== Biography ==
Adam Höhn was born in Germany on 30 November 1875, the son of Jacob Höhn and Margaretha Schmidt.<ref name="fag_adam">Find a Grave, database and images (https://www.findagrave.com/memorial/133020376/adam-hohn : accessed 17 November 2026), memorial 133020376, Adam Hohn (30 Nov 1875-5 Jul 1902), All Faiths Cemetery, Middle Village, Queens, New York.</ref><ref name="c1900hohn">"1900 United States Federal Census", database with images, Ancestry (https://www.ancestry.com/search/collections/7602/records/66919373 : accessed 17 November 2026), Jacob Hohn household, 833 First Avenue, Manhattan, New York, New York; enumeration district (ED) 589, sheet 7, lines 93-96; NARA microfilm publication T623, roll 1107. Daughter indexed as "Horn Hohn" (name and relationship columns transposed on the image; she is "Annie", daughter).</ref> He probably came to New York with his parents on the ''Rhynland'' in August 1883.<ref name="ship1883">"New York, U.S., Arriving Passenger and Crew Lists (including Castle Garden and Ellis Island), 1820-1957", database with images, Ancestry (https://www.ancestry.com/search/collections/7488/records/11769566 : accessed 17 November 2026), Jacob Hohn, 32, with Mary Hohn, 26, and Adam Hohn, 8; ship Rhynland, Antwerp to New York, arrived 10 Aug 1883; NARA microfilm publication M237, roll 469.</ref> In 1900 he was 20, single, and working as a grocer with his father at 833 First Avenue in Manhattan.<ref name="c1900hohn" /> He died in Manhattan on 5 July 1902, aged 26, and was buried in the Lutheran (now All Faiths) Cemetery in Middle Village, Queens. His mother was buried beside him in 1906.<ref name="d1902adam">"New York, New York, U.S., Extracted Death Index, 1862-1948", database, Ancestry (https://www.ancestry.com/search/collections/9131/records/1557712 : accessed 17 November 2026), Adam Hohn, age 25, died 5 Jul 1902, Manhattan, certificate 20097.</ref><ref name="fag_margaretha">Find a Grave, database and images (https://www.findagrave.com/memorial/133020303/margaretha-hohn : accessed 17 November 2026), memorial 133020303, Margaretha Hohn (18 Nov 1856-27 May 1906), All Faiths Cemetery, Middle Village, Queens, New York; gravestone photograph by Lisa F. (inscription: "meine geliebte Gattin Margaretha Höhn ... und Sohn Adam Höhn").</ref>
